one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent adopted a two-tier probability distribution parameterization (k high-prob + rest low-prob) that lacks sufficient degrees of freedom to simultaneously satisfy KL(P||U)=10 and KL(U||P)=10, then repeatedly iterated on this same flawed strategy while saving noncompliant outputs and ultimately submitting despite explicit tolerance failures.
t_err_evidence: Step 5: Agent rewrites the solver using a two-tier distribution (k high-prob tokens + rest uniform low-prob) as its primary strategy after numpy/scipy are unavailable. This false premise -- that such a two-tier distribution has enough free parameters to satisfy both KL divergences simultaneously at target 10.0 -- is the decisive wrong belief. The step analysis also flags an invalid .npy format in the initial version.
t_commit_evidence: Step 9: After running the refined binary-search solver, the best achievable result is forward_kl=9.971524 (error 0.028) and backward_kl=9.993806 (error 0.006) -- still outside the 0.001 tolerance. This is the closest the two-tier approach ever gets; all subsequent attempts (steps 10-27) stay within the same paradigm and fail to converge, locking in the failing outcome.
t_surface_evidence: Step 6: First execution of the two-tier solver shows 'Best error found: 0.105041' with forward_kl=10.308074 (error 0.308) and backward_kl=10.100652 (error 0.101), both clearly outside the 0.001 tolerance. The file is saved anyway, making the failure observable.
trigger_explanation: After discovering numpy/scipy are unavailable, the agent assumes that a two-tier distribution (k tokens with high probability p_h, remaining tokens with low probability p_l) is a sufficient parameterization for the optimization problem. In reality, a two-tier distribution has only one free parameter (p_h, given k), so the two KL divergences trace a one-dimensional curve in (KL_forward, KL_backward) space that does not pass through the target point (10, 10) within tolerance for any value of k tried. The agent never recognizes this mathematical impossibility and instead keeps refining the search within the wrong family of distributions.
forewarning_evidence: Step 6 output: 'Best error found: 0.105041, Forward KL error: 0.308074, Backward KL error: 0.100652' -- both errors far exceed 0.001 tolerance, yet the distribution is saved. Step 9 shows the best possible result still outside tolerance (errors 0.028 and 0.006). Step 13 shows backward_kl stuck at ~4.60 for most configurations, far from target 10.0.
